original_question: Understand the critical solutions and critical behavior that arise at the threshold of black hole formation in gravitational collapse within general relativity, especially beyond highly symmetric settings.
target_in_paper: Section 6, Problem CMP3: "Understand critical phenomena in gravitational collapse in GR," together with the immediately preceding paragraph that sets up one-parameter families of coupled Einstein-matter solutions and the threshold self-similar solution.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's target as critical phenomena at the threshold of black-hole formation in general relativity, and it also preserves the paper's explicit emphasis on understanding the critical solution and critical behavior beyond symmetry-reduced settings.
missing_details: The paper frames the problem through one-parameter families of solutions to the coupled Einstein-matter equations, labeled by a continuous parameter p.
The prescribed initial data depend on p, and p controls the strength of the initially imploding matter.

The two comparison regimes should be stated: for small p the spacetime remains regular everywhere (for example, massless radiation disperses to infinity), while for large p some matter is trapped within a singular black hole.
At some critical value of p, there is a critical self-similar solution corresponding to the threshold of black-hole formation.
The paper notes evidence that virtually any collapse model admitting black-hole formation exhibits such critical behavior; this universality claim is part of the nearby context.

The official formulation is the narrower "Understand critical phenomena in gravitational collapse in GR," so the question should stay within gravitational collapse in GR rather than broadening to loosely related black-hole-threshold questions.
The no-symmetry emphasis should be retained explicitly as the especially difficult case: "especially in the case in which there are no symmetries."

No sharper mathematical hypotheses are supplied here: the paper does not fix a specific matter model, gauge, asymptotic class, operator, ring or field, homogeneity or degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or theorem-style quantifier, so those should not be invented.
refined_question: For collapse models in general relativity that admit black-hole formation, consider one-parameter families of solutions to the coupled Einstein-matter equations whose prescribed initial data depend continuously on a parameter p measuring the strength of initially imploding matter, so that small p leads to globally regular or dispersive evolution and large p leads to a singular black hole. At the critical value of p corresponding to the threshold of black-hole formation, there is a critical self-similar solution. The research question is: understand and characterize this critical solution and the associated critical phenomena in gravitational collapse in GR, especially in cases with no assumed symmetries.
justification: This is the nearest official formulation of your draft in the paper. The exact open problem is Problem CMP3 in Section 6, and the immediately preceding paragraph is essential because it supplies the paper's only concrete setup for what "critical phenomena" means here: a continuous parameter p in families of coupled Einstein-matter solutions, a small-p regular or dispersive regime, a large-p black-hole regime, and a critical self-similar threshold solution. Your draft already captures the threshold-of-black-hole-formation theme and the emphasis beyond symmetry assumptions, but it omits the one-parameter Einstein-matter setup and the explicit self-similar nature of the critical solution, which are the key paper-faithful details needed to make the question stand alone.
